patch.value: The .cmd shim resolvePmBin selects on win32 cannot be launched by its only caller

resolvePmBin deliberately returns the node_modules/.bin/pm.cmd batch shim on win32 because Windows cannot execute the extensionless POSIX shim. But fetchAllItems passes that return value straight to spawnSync with no shell/command-processor option. Since the CVE-2024-27980 hardening landed (Node 18.20+, 20.12+), Node refuses to execute .cmd/.bat via spawnSync without a shell and fails with EINVAL. So on the exact platform the .cmd branch exists to support, every pm list-all read fails to spawn and every standup export/post aborts, even though the project-local CLI is installed. The resolution decision (use the .cmd) and the launch decision (how to spawn) live in different places and disagree.

value.note: 132 tests pass; includes exact per-platform launch argv (win32+.cmd,win32+extensionless,linux),ComSpec honoring + fallback,PATH-fallback wrapping,and the POSIX metacharacter argv round trip

value.text: author=pi-agent,text=Root cause confirmed by inspection of every spawn site: index.ts has exactly one child-process call that consumes resolvePmBin value — fetchAllItems spawnSync (no spawn/execFile elsewhere). The resolver picked pm.cmd on win32 while the caller spawned that path directly with no command processor; since the CVE-2024-27980 hardening (Node 18.20+/20.12+) spawnSync refuses .cmd/.bat without a shell and fails EINVAL, so every standup read aborts on Windows. Fix collapses the two decisions into one place: new pmLaunchPlan(bin, platform) returns {command, prefixArgs} — on win32 spawn ComSpec (default cmd.exe) with ["/d","/s","/c", bin]; elsewhere spawn bin directly with an empty prefix, byte-for-byte the old POSIX invocation. resolvePmBin(moduleUrl, platform) now returns that PmLaunch (platform injectable, same pattern as moduleUrl), and fetchAllItems accepts PmLaunch or a path string, normalizing strings through the same pmLaunchPlan so no caller can bypass the launch decision. No shell:true anywhere: arguments stay discrete argv elements with windowsVerbatimArguments:false, so Node quotes each one itself and metacharacters reach pm as data. Tests: exact argv for win32+.cmd, win32+extensionless, linux; ComSpec honored/fallback; bare-pm PATH fallback wrapped on win32; and a real-subprocess metacharacter test (root containing space & quote | pipe) proving it arrives as ONE argv element. Revert experiments: full revert of index.ts fails the suite at import (pmLaunchPlan no longer exported); surgical revert of just the ComSpec wrapping fails 4 tests with command collapsing to the bare pm.cmd path and the /d /s /c prefix missing. npm run release:check green; coverage 89.05/87.43/90.35 (baseline 88.64/87.07/90.27), thresholds untouched.

Root cause confirmed by inspecting every spawn site: index.ts has exactly one child-process call that consumes resolvePmBin's value — fetchAllItems' spawnSync (no spawn/execFile anywhere else). The resolver picked pm.cmd on win32 while the caller spawned that path directly with no command processor; since the CVE-2024-27980 hardening (Node 18.20+/20.12+) spawnSync refuses .cmd/.bat without a shell and fails EINVAL, every standup read aborted on Windows.

Fix collapses the two decisions into one place. New pmLaunchPlan(bin, platform) returns {command, prefixArgs}: on win32 spawn ComSpec (default cmd.exe) with ["/d","/s","/c", bin]; everywhere else spawn bin directly with an empty prefix — byte-for-byte the old POSIX invocation. resolvePmBin(moduleUrl, platform) now returns that PmLaunch (platform injectable, same pattern as moduleUrl), and fetchAllItems accepts a PmLaunch or a path string, normalizing strings through the same pmLaunchPlan so no caller can bypass the launch decision. No shell:true anywhere: arguments stay discrete argv elements with windowsVerbatimArguments:false, so Node quotes each one itself and metacharacters reach pm as data.

Tests: exact argv for win32+.cmd, win32+extensionless, and linux; ComSpec honored plus cmd.exe fallback; bare-pm PATH fallback wrapped on win32; and a real-subprocess metacharacter test (a root containing space, &, ", and |) proving it arrives as ONE argv element. Revert experiments: a full revert of index.ts fails the suite at import (pmLaunchPlan no longer exported); a surgical revert of just the ComSpec wrapping fails 4 tests with command collapsing to the bare pm.cmd path and the /d /s /c prefix missing. npm run release:check green; coverage 89.05/87.43/90.35 (baseline 88.64/87.07/90.27), thresholds untouched.

patch.value: resolvePmBin now returns a PmLaunch {command, prefixArgs} built by the new pmLaunchPlan(bin, platform): on win32 the spawn targets the ComSpec command processor (cmd.exe fallback) with ["/d","/s","/c", bin] ahead of the pm arguments; everywhere else it spawns the resolved binary directly with an empty prefix, byte-for-byte the previous POSIX invocation. fetchAllItems consumes that plan for both its default and its string parameter (strings normalize through the same pmLaunchPlan), so the resolution decision and the launch decision can no longer disagree. No shell:true anywhere; arguments remain discrete argv elements with windowsVerbatimArguments:false so Node quotes each one itself.

The .cmd shim resolvePmBin selects on win32 is launched through a command processor, so a project-local pm read succeeds on Windows; POSIX launches are unchanged; no argument metacharacter is ever interpreted by a shell.

Verified without a Windows box by platform injection: exact argv asserted for win32+.cmd (cmd.exe /d /s /c <pm.cmd> --path ... list-all --json --include-body), win32+extensionless, and linux (bare shim, no prefix); a real-subprocess test passes a root containing space & quote | pipe and observes it arrive as one discrete argv element. Revert checks: full index.ts revert fails the suite at import; surgical revert of the ComSpec wrapping fails the four launch tests. npm run release:check green; coverage 89.05/87.43/90.35 (baseline 88.64/87.07/90.27).
pm list-all reads on win32 spawn through ComSpec instead of failing EINVAL on the bare .cmd shim; 132/132 tests pass; release:check green.
